title: TRIBE
scope: McMahon 2016 TRIBE implementation, as represented by the Illumina TRIBE schematic and the TRIBE row of the additional poster. The target is RBP-interacting RNA; the mark is an internal RNA A-to-I edit and the depicted final carrier is RNA-derived cDNA with a G sequence signature. The single route comprises fusion construction, cell-specific expression and binding, RNA editing, and broad cDNA preparation. Other poster rows and the adjacent standalone inosine drawing are outside this workflow. The endogenous ADAR cartoon is a domain/mechanism illustration, not an alternative target workflow. This architecture records editing evidence rather than crosslink-based capture.

evidence.quote: TRIBE flies were generated by cloning the RBP-ADARcd-V5 transgene into a modified pJFRC7-20x UAS construct (RBP in locus of removed mCD8-GFP, Addgene #26220), which was injected by BestGene (Chino Hills, CA).

Because the double stranded RNA-binding (dsRBD) regions of ADAR are missing from the fusion protein, its editing specificity is determined by the RNA recognition features of the RBP; target transcripts are edited in vivo and then identified by RNA sequencing (Figure 1).

operations.label: Mark target RNA by proximal A-to-I editing
operations.description: The RNA-bound fusion catalyzes conversion of an editable RNA adenosine to inosine. The next boundary shows the RNA mark after the interaction; it does not establish a protein-removal procedure.
operations.mechanism: The tethered ADAR catalytic domain deaminates adenosine within target RNA to inosine. An editable proximal A and suitable RNA context constrain marking; the catalytic domain retains a strong preference for double-stranded RNA.
operations.information_effect: The persistent internal RNA edit records a transcript interaction. In the studied Hrp48 implementation, editing usually occurs near rather than at the RBP binding site. Some bound targets remain unedited, so absence of a mark does not exclude interaction.

evidence.quote: This suggests that TRIBE usually edits near but not at the binding site, consistent with fusion of the editing moiety to the C-terminus of Hrp48. However, some more distant editing might be due to RNA flexibility and/or the dsRNA preference of the ADARcd (see Discussion).

Obviously the ADARcd-TRIBE protein has an absolute requirement for an editable substrate (an adenosine) proximal to the RBP binding site, the absence of which may preclude the editing of some targets and result in false negatives.

However the most prominent cause of false negatives is probably the strong preference of the ADAR catalytic domain for double-stranded RNA even without its dsRBDs (Macbeth et al., 2005, Eggington et al., 2011, Montiel-Gonzalez et al., 2013, Vogel et al., 2014, Vogel and Stafforst, 2014, Phelps et al., 2015).

operations.label: Recover cellular RNA and prepare a cDNA library
operations.description: The arrow from I-marked RNA to cDNA is a broad RNA-recovery and cDNA-preparation interface. RNA from the expressing cells is used to generate the RNA-derived cDNA library; this is not a depicted affinity selection of fusion-bound transcripts. The figure ends at cDNA and does not show a separate sequencing-data boundary.
operations.mechanism: RNA is recovered and reverse-transcribed for cDNA library preparation. The RNA A-to-I event is represented as an A-to-G sequence difference in transcript orientation. The diagram does not specify first-strand polarity or internal library-preparation steps; the primary paper uses different preparations for S2 cells and manually sorted neurons.
operations.information_effect: Subsequent RNA sequencing can identify source transcripts with novel editing marks. Genomic sequence and non-TRIBE controls distinguish genomic variation and endogenous RNA editing from introduced marks. The panel supports an RNA-derived cDNA carrier, not an RBP-containing sequencing library, exact contact mapping, or exhaustive detection of all targets.

evidence.quote: Endogenous Drosophila ADAR is a modular enzyme consisting of two double-stranded RNA-binding domains (dsRBDs) as well as a catalytic domain, which deaminates adenosine to inosine (Bass and Weintraub, 1988, Keegan et al., 2004). Inosine is recognized as guanosine both in vitro and in vivo.

Importantly, the editing event is irreversible, marking the target RNA permanently after the interaction. No biochemistry is required, RNA is simply extracted from cells of interest and sequenced. Novel editing events define RNA targets, namely, transcripts that interacted with the fusion protein.
They are confined to the correct base conversion, A to G (data not shown), indicating that the fusion protein is catalyzing the appropriate deamination reaction.

method_scopes.rationale: The card title, the collection heading and caption, and the explicitly labelled poster row identify TRIBE alone. The leftmost highlighted RBP–RNA icon illustrates the assay goal; it is not a separate transformation or a selected RNA preparation. McMahon et al. describes the matching RBP–Drosophila-ADARcd implementation. All four operations apply at this schematic scope; create_fusion uses the primary genetic-construct interface to interpret the fusion-engineering cartoon. CLIP, RBNS and HITS-RAP are neighboring/background assays, not alternative TRIBE branches. The schematic stops at cDNA, so RNA sequencing and editing interpretation are explained as the downstream use of that carrier rather than expanded into unshown processing operations. The exact library-preparation recipe is not assigned universally across the paper's cell-culture and neuronal applications.

evidence.quote: To address these issues, we developed TRIBE (Targets of RNA-binding proteins Identified By Editing), a technique that couples an RBP to the catalytic domain of the Drosophila RNA editing enzyme ADAR and expresses the fusion protein in vivo. RBP targets are marked with novel RNA editing events and identified by sequencing RNA.

Because the double stranded RNA-binding (dsRBD) regions of ADAR are missing from the fusion protein, its editing specificity is determined by the RNA recognition features of the RBP; target transcripts are edited in vivo and then identified by RNA sequencing (Figure 1).

TRIBE flies were generated by cloning the RBP-ADARcd-V5 transgene into a modified pJFRC7-20x UAS construct (RBP in locus of removed mCD8-GFP, Addgene #26220), which was injected by BestGene (Chino Hills, CA).

Fluorescently labelled neurons were isolated from dissected, triturated fly brains by manual sorting using a glass micro-pipette, as described in Abruzzi et al. (2015). RNA sequencing libraries from S2 cells were constructed using the standard Illumina Truseq kit protocol. RNA-sequencing libraries from manually sorted neurons were made as described in Abruzzi et al. (2015).

B) Native Drosophila ADAR is composed of two double stranded RNA-binding domains (dsRBDs) that mediates its target specificity, and a deaminase domain that catalyzes adenosine to inosine conversion. C) The dsRBDs of ADAR are replaced with the RBP of interest.

corrections.primary_statement: In the Hrp48-TRIBE results, the paper states that editing usually occurs near but not at the binding site; some edits can be more distant. Use the primary interpretation: an RNA edit and its G sequence signature mark an interacting transcript and an editing coordinate, not necessarily the exact RBP contact nucleotide.
